text:
maria-support: Customer Inkdot reported a spike of 200–400ms tail latency from EU users and intermittent 401s starting ~09:10 UTC. They say traffic is landing in us-west instead of ams/frankfurt. :frowning:

aj-eng: Copy. Any recent rollouts? Did geoip DB sync finish?

cloudbot: geoip-sync: started 2024-12-18T08:02:01Z, completed 2024-12-18T08:05:12Z (s3://redwood-geoip/2024-12-18.tar.gz) :white_check_mark:

liam-oncall: Looking at ingress logs — I see a bunch of requests from resolver 89.12.34.1 with answer IP 34.12.56.78 (us-west). The resolver TTL on our edge DNS was 86400 for that name, last updated 2024-12-17. Could be ISP prefetch/coalescing.

inkdot-customer: attaching dig from one affected user in Amsterdam: ```; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.com A
34.12.56.78
; query time: 23 msec
; SERVER: 8.8.8.8#53(8.8.8.8)\n``` The user sees 401s intermittently until 1–2 minutes later when it corrects to 3.210.45.10 (ams).

aj-eng: That dig shows their resolver (8.8.8.8) returns our us-west IP. Two working hypotheses: 1) upstream resolver is coalescing / prefetching and using an old mapping in its cache that points to us-west; 2) EDNS/Client-Subnet stripped or NAT translation causing wrong geoip decision on our edge.

liam-oncall: I pulled edge access logs for the token failures — requests arriving to us-west had X-Region header missing and token validation looked up in redis shard eu-1 (which is region-scoped) so auth fails if token was issued in eu shard. That explains the 401s.

aj-eng: Repro steps for support to ask the customer to run (cheap): ```# from affected client
$ dig +short @<their_resolver> api.redwood.com A
$ dig +trace api.redwood.com
$ curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.com/health -H 'Host: api.redwood.com'```
Include the resolver IP and AS number (whois). Also ask them to run from a mobile ISP if possible.

network-sre: This looks like resolver prefetch + NAT coalescing at ISP edge. Many ISPs prefetch popular hostnames and map to a single proxy IP; if that proxy sits in a different region our geoip lookup will misclassify due to the NAT public IP being mapped to a US PoP. We saw similar during the 2024-09 CDN migration. Immediate mitigation options: lower DNS TTL for api.redwood.com for EU hosts (to 60s) while we invalidate geoip cache and push a targeted route override for that resolver ASN.

maria-support: Can SRE run the geoip invalidation and push the override? Also asking customer for packet capture of client->resolver (if they can) or at least curl + resolve output.

network-sre: Running invalidate: ```infra-tool geoip-invalidate --asn 12345 --region eu --note "inkdot incident"``` — queued. Also applying temporary routing override: ```infra-tool route-override --prefix 89.12.0.0/16 --prefer-pop ams```. Will monitor. :eyes: 

cloudbot: route-override: started by @network-sre 2024-12-18T09:36:42Z — changes will take effect within 30s.

liam-oncall: After override applied, I see subsequent lookups from resolver 89.12.34.1 resolving to 3.210.45.10 (ams) and auth success rate back to normal. Latency dropped to baseline.

maria-support: Customer confirmed degraded UX fixed for now. We'll keep the TTL low and request ISP to clear their prefetch cache. Need postmortem: assign to network-sre + eng to document mitigation and add automations to detect resolver-asn mapping flips.

aj-eng: Notes for postmortem: add resolver ASN telemetry to alert when percentage of requests from a resolver ASN crossing region > 5% and implement automatic short-TTL rollback + route-override playbook.

maria-support: Thanks all — moving to incident channel for postmortem write-up. :thumbsup:
